summary: On the floor, the speaker argues a minimum wage bill through named kinds of people and their bills, in the plain speech of a neighbor who knows them.
realLife: In a floor debate on a bill to cap minimum wage increases, senators spoke of families living paycheck to paycheck in their own town, students they coach who leave practice early to work, and the gap between a wage and rent, groceries and child care. A veteran senator years earlier pressed the same point more sharply, accusing colleagues of pleasing business groups at the poor's expense.
sources: Nebraska state senator Quick, floor debate on LB258, Apr 1, 2025: https://nebraskalegislature.gov/FloorDocs/109/PDF/Transcripts/FloorDebate/r1day54.pdf
